{
  float new_dw;
  int k, j;
  ly[0] = 1.0;

#ifdef OPEN
  omp_set_num_threads(NUM_THREAD);
  #pragma omp parallel for  \
      shared(oldw, w, delta) \
	  private(j, k, new_dw) \
	  firstprivate(ndelta, nly, momentum) 
#endif 
  for (j = 1; j <= ndelta; j++) {
    for (k = 0; k <= nly; k++) {
      new_dw = ((ETA * delta[j] * ly[k]) + (MOMENTUM * oldw[k][j]));
	  w[k][j] += new_dw;
	  oldw[k][j] = new_dw;
    }
  }
}


void bpnn_feedforward(BPNN *net)
{
  int in, hid, out;

  in = net->input_n;
  hid = net->hidden_n;
  out = net->output_n;

  /*** Feed forward input activations. ***/
  bpnn_layerforward(net->input_units, net->hidden_units,
      net->input_weights, in, hid);
  bpnn_layerforward(net->hidden_units, net->output_units,
      net->hidden_weights, hid, out);

}


void bpnn_train(BPNN *net, float *eo, float *eh)
{
  int in, hid, out;
  float out_err, hid_err;

  in = net->input_n;
  hid = net->hidden_n;
  out = net->output_n;

  /*** Feed forward input activations. ***/
  bpnn_layerforward(net->input_units, net->hidden_units,
      net->input_weights, in, hid);
  bpnn_layerforward(net->hidden_units, net->output_units,
      net->hidden_weights, hid, out);

  /*** Compute error on output and hidden units. ***/
  bpnn_output_error(net->output_delta, net->target, net->output_units,
      out, &out_err);
  bpnn_hidden_error(net->hidden_delta, hid, net->output_delta, out,
      net->hidden_weights, net->hidden_units, &hid_err);
  *eo = out_err;
  *eh = hid_err;

  /*** Adjust input and hidden weights. ***/
  bpnn_adjust_weights(net->output_delta, out, net->hidden_units, hid,
      net->hidden_weights, net->hidden_prev_weights);
  bpnn_adjust_weights(net->hidden_delta, hid, net->input_units, in,
      net->input_weights, net->input_prev_weights);

}




void bpnn_save(BPNN *net, char *filename)
{
  int n1, n2, n3, i, j, memcnt;
  float dvalue, **w;
  char *mem;
  ///add//
  FILE *pFile;
  pFile = fopen( filename, "w+" );
  ///////
  /*
  if ((fd = creat(filename, 0644)) == -1) {
    printf("BPNN_SAVE: Cannot create '%s'\n", filename);
    return;
  }
  */

  n1 = net->input_n;  n2 = net->hidden_n;  n3 = net->output_n;
  printf("Saving %dx%dx%d network to '%s'\n", n1, n2, n3, filename);
  //fflush(stdout);

  //write(fd, (char *) &n1, sizeof(int));
  //write(fd, (char *) &n2, sizeof(int));
  //write(fd, (char *) &n3, sizeof(int));

  fwrite( (char *) &n1 , sizeof(char), sizeof(char), pFile);
  fwrite( (char *) &n2 , sizeof(char), sizeof(char), pFile);
  fwrite( (char *) &n3 , sizeof(char), sizeof(char), pFile);

  

  memcnt = 0;
  w = net->input_weights;
  mem = (char *) malloc ((unsigned) ((n1+1) * (n2+1) * sizeof(float)));
  for (i = 0; i <= n1; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <= n2; j++) {
      dvalue = w[i][j];
      fastcopy(&mem[memcnt], &dvalue, sizeof(float));
      memcnt += sizeof(float);
    }
  }
  //write(fd, mem, (n1+1) * (n2+1) * sizeof(float));
  fwrite( mem , (unsigned)(sizeof(float)), (unsigned) ((n1+1) * (n2+1) * sizeof(float)) , pFile);
  free(mem);

  memcnt = 0;
  w = net->hidden_weights;
  mem = (char *) malloc ((unsigned) ((n2+1) * (n3+1) * sizeof(float)));
  for (i = 0; i <= n2; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <= n3; j++) {
      dvalue = w[i][j];
      fastcopy(&mem[memcnt], &dvalue, sizeof(float));
      memcnt += sizeof(float);
    }
  }
  //write(fd, mem, (n2+1) * (n3+1) * sizeof(float));
  fwrite( mem , sizeof(float), (unsigned) ((n2+1) * (n3+1) * sizeof(float)) , pFile);
  free(mem);

  fclose(pFile);
  return;
}


BPNN *bpnn_read(char *filename)
{
  char *mem;
  BPNN *new_t;
  int fd, n1, n2, n3, i, j, memcnt;

  if ((fd = open(filename, 0, 0644)) == -1) {
    return (NULL);
  }

  printf("Reading '%s'\n", filename);  //fflush(stdout);

  read(fd, (char *) &n1, sizeof(int));
  read(fd, (char *) &n2, sizeof(int));
  read(fd, (char *) &n3, sizeof(int));
  new_t = bpnn_internal_create(n1, n2, n3);

  printf("'%s' contains a %dx%dx%d network\n", filename, n1, n2, n3);
  printf("Reading input weights...");  //fflush(stdout);

  memcnt = 0;
  mem = (char *) malloc ((unsigned) ((n1+1) * (n2+1) * sizeof(float)));
  read(fd, mem, (n1+1) * (n2+1) * sizeof(float));
  for (i = 0; i <= n1; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <= n2; j++) {
      fastcopy(&(new_t->input_weights[i][j]), &mem[memcnt], sizeof(float));
      memcnt += sizeof(float);
    }
  }
  free(mem);

  printf("Done\nReading hidden weights...");  //fflush(stdout);

  memcnt = 0;
  mem = (char *) malloc ((unsigned) ((n2+1) * (n3+1) * sizeof(float)));
  read(fd, mem, (n2+1) * (n3+1) * sizeof(float));
  for (i = 0; i <= n2; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <= n3; j++) {
      fastcopy(&(new_t->hidden_weights[i][j]), &mem[memcnt], sizeof(float));
      memcnt += sizeof(float);
    }
  }
  free(mem);
  close(fd);

  printf("Done\n");  //fflush(stdout);

  bpnn_zero_weights(new_t->input_prev_weights, n1, n2);
  bpnn_zero_weights(new_t->hidden_prev_weights, n2, n3);

  return (new_t);
}

// includes, system
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <sys/time.h>
#include <omp.h>
#include "backprop.h"
#include "reference.h"

double get_time() {
  struct timeval t;
  gettimeofday(&t,NULL);
  return t.tv_sec+t.tv_usec*1e-6;
}

unsigned int num_threads = 0;
unsigned int num_blocks = 0;

////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// Program main
////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
int main( int argc, char** argv) 
{
  setup(argc, argv);
  return 0;
}

int bpnn_train_kernel(BPNN *net, float *eo, float *eh)
{
  int in, hid, out;
  float out_err, hid_err;

  in = net->input_n;
  hid = net->hidden_n;
  out = net->output_n;   

  float *input_weights_one_dim;
  float *input_weights_one_dim_r;
  float *input_weights_prev_one_dim;
  float * partial_sum;
  float sum;
  unsigned int num_blocks = in / BLOCK_SIZE;

  input_weights_one_dim = (float *) malloc((in + 1)* (hid + 1) * sizeof(float));
  input_weights_one_dim_r = (float *) malloc((in + 1)* (hid + 1) * sizeof(float));
  input_weights_prev_one_dim = (float *) malloc((in + 1)* (hid + 1) * sizeof(float));
  partial_sum = (float *) malloc(num_blocks * WIDTH * sizeof(float));


  // this preprocessing stage is temporarily added to correct the bug of wrong memcopy using two-dimensional net->inputweights
  // todo: fix mem allocation
  int m = 0;
  for (int k = 0; k <= in; k++) {  
    for (int j = 0; j <= hid; j++) {
      input_weights_one_dim[m] = net->input_weights[k][j];
      input_weights_one_dim_r[m] = net->input_weights[k][j];
      input_weights_prev_one_dim[m] = net-> input_prev_weights[k][j];
      m++;
    }
  }

  printf("Performing device offload\n");

  double offload_start = get_time();

  float* input = net->input_units;
  float* input_weights = input_weights_one_dim;
  float* input_prev_weights = input_weights_prev_one_dim;
  float* hidden_delta = net->hidden_delta;

  #pragma omp target data map(to: input[0:in+1], \
                                  hidden_delta[0:hid+1], \
                                  input_prev_weights[0:(in+1)*(hid+1)]) \
                          map(tofrom: input_weights[0:(in+1)*(hid+1)]) \
                          map(alloc: partial_sum[0:num_blocks*WIDTH]) 
  {
    #pragma omp target teams num_teams(num_blocks) thread_limit(BLOCK_SIZE*BLOCK_SIZE)
    {
      float input_node[HEIGHT];
      float weight_matrix [HEIGHT * WIDTH];
      #pragma omp parallel
      {
        int by = omp_get_team_num();
        int tx = omp_get_thread_num() % BLOCK_SIZE;
        int ty = omp_get_thread_num() / BLOCK_SIZE;
        
        int index = ( hid + 1 ) * HEIGHT * by + ( hid + 1 ) * ty + tx + 1 + ( hid + 1 ) ;  
        
        int index_in = HEIGHT * by + ty + 1;
        
        if ( tx == 0 )
          input_node[ty] = input[index_in] ;
        #pragma omp barrier
        
        weight_matrix[ty * WIDTH + tx] =  input_weights[index];
        #pragma omp barrier
        
        weight_matrix[ty * WIDTH + tx]= weight_matrix[ty * WIDTH + tx] * input_node[ty];
        #pragma omp barrier
        
        for ( int i = 1 ; i <= HEIGHT ; i=i*2){
          int power_two = i; 
        
          if( ty % power_two == 0 )
          weight_matrix[ty * WIDTH + tx]= weight_matrix[ty * WIDTH + tx] + weight_matrix[(ty + power_two/2)* WIDTH + tx];
        
          #pragma omp barrier
        
        }
        
        input_weights[index] =  weight_matrix[ty * WIDTH + tx];
        
        #pragma omp barrier
        
        if ( tx == 0 ) {
          partial_sum[by * hid + ty] = weight_matrix[tx* WIDTH + ty];
        }
      }
    }
    
    #pragma omp target update from(partial_sum[0:num_blocks*WIDTH])
        for (int j = 1; j <= hid; j++) {
          sum = 0.0;
          for (int k = 0; k < num_blocks; k++) {  
            sum += partial_sum[k * hid + j-1] ;
          }
    #ifdef DEBUG
          printf("j=%d sum=%f\n", j,sum);
    #endif
          sum += net->input_weights[0][j];
          net-> hidden_units[j] = float(1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-sum)));
        }
    
        bpnn_layerforward(net->hidden_units, net->output_units, net->hidden_weights, hid, out);
        bpnn_output_error(net->output_delta, net->target, net->output_units, out, &out_err);
        bpnn_hidden_error(net->hidden_delta, hid, net->output_delta, out, net->hidden_weights, net->hidden_units, &hid_err);  
        bpnn_adjust_weights(net->output_delta, out, net->hidden_units, hid, net->hidden_weights, net->hidden_prev_weights);
    
        // input_weights has been written in the first kernel, so it needs to be restored.
    #pragma omp target update to(input_weights[0:(in+1)*(hid+1)])
    
    #pragma omp target teams num_teams(num_blocks) thread_limit(BLOCK_SIZE*BLOCK_SIZE)
    {
      #pragma omp parallel
      {
        int by = omp_get_team_num();
        int tx = omp_get_thread_num() % BLOCK_SIZE;
        int ty = omp_get_thread_num() / BLOCK_SIZE;
        
        int index =  ( hid + 1 ) * HEIGHT * by + ( hid + 1 ) * ty + tx + 1 + ( hid + 1 ) ;  
        int index_y = HEIGHT * by + ty + 1;
        int index_x = tx + 1;
        
        input_weights[index] += ((ETA * hidden_delta[index_x] * input[index_y]) + (MOMENTUM * input_prev_weights[index]));
        input_prev_weights[index] = ((ETA * hidden_delta[index_x] * input[index_y]) + (MOMENTUM * input_prev_weights[index]));
        
        #pragma omp barrier
        
        if (ty == 0 && by ==0){
          input_weights[index_x] += ((ETA * hidden_delta[index_x]) + (MOMENTUM * input_prev_weights[index_x]));
          input_prev_weights[index_x] = ((ETA * hidden_delta[index_x]) + (MOMENTUM * input_prev_weights[index_x]));
        }
      } 
    }
  } 
  double offload_end = get_time();
  printf("Device offloading time = %lf(s)\n", offload_end - offload_start);

  reference (in, hid, out, net, 
             input_weights_one_dim_r,
             input_weights_prev_one_dim,
             partial_sum); 

  bool ok = true;
  for (int i = 0; i < (in+1)*(hid+1); i++) {
    if (fabsf(input_weights_one_dim[i] - input_weights_one_dim_r[i]) >= 1e-3f) {
      ok = false;
      break;
    }
  }
  printf("%s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");

#ifdef OUTPUT
  for (int i = 0; i < (in+1); i++) 
    printf("i=%d input_units=%f\n", i, net->input_units[i]);
  for (int i = 0; i < (in+1)*(hid+1); i++) 
    printf("i=%d input_weights=%f\n", i,input_weights_one_dim[i]);
#endif
  free(input_weights_prev_one_dim);
  free(partial_sum);
  free(input_weights_one_dim);
  free(input_weights_one_dim_r);

  return 0;
}

args.fp32_flop_explanation: Only the first target teams kernel is counted. Per thread it executes one multiply for `weight_matrix[...] * input_node[ty]`; then the reduction loop runs for `i=1,2,4,8,16`, and because `ty % power_two == 0` is true for all threads when `i=1`, for 128 threads when `i=2`, 64 when `i=4`, 32 when `i=8`, and 16 when `i=16`, this gives 256+128+64+32+16 = 496 FP32 adds per team; adding 256 multiplies gives 752 FP32 FLOPs per team. args.dram_bytes_read_explanation: For the first kernel, compulsory global reads come from `input[index_in]` for `tx==0` only (16 floats per team) and `input_weights[index]` for every thread (256 floats per team). The __cuda_sm70_barrier_sync_7_count HFMA2 is called from divergent paths (BRA.DIV) which are rarely taken in practice for well-formed warps. For the main path with 256 threads per block, the block size equals the thread_limit so the code takes the path where all threads participate and the barrier sync helper is not called. Weight reads: 4,194,304 bytes / 128 = 32,768 cache lines = 4,194,304 bytes. Total DRAM read ≈ 4,456,448 bytes.

prediction.blockSz_explanation: The same OpenMP launch uses `thread_limit(BLOCK_SIZE*BLOCK_SIZE)` with `BLOCK_SIZE=16`, giving 256 threads per team. The SASS uses `SR_TID.X` directly and derives `tx = tid % 16`, `ty = tid / 16`, consistent with a 1D CUDA block of 256 threads.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: Per team, the kernel executes one FP32 multiply for every thread (`FMUL`, 256 total), one extra `FADD R3,R0,R0` for every thread from the compiler-lowered first reduction step (256 adds), and four conditional reduction adds for subsets of threads: 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 = 240 `FADD`s, matching the SASS. Thus each team performs 256 + 256 + 240 = 752 FP32 FLOPs, and across 4096 teams that is 752*4096 = 3,080,192 FP32 FLOPs for the first invocation.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: Neither the source for this offload region nor the taken-path SASS contains double-precision arithmetic instructions; all arithmetic is single-precision plus compiler-generated packed-half helper ops. Therefore the first invocation performs no FP64 FLOPs.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The SASS contains a compiler-generated `HFMA2.MMA` used to materialize the 4-byte scaling factor before address calculation, executed once per thread in the main kernel body. Counting it as real FP16 arithmetic per the rules gives 4 FP16 FLOPs per thread, so 256*4096*4 = 4,194,304 FP16 FLOPs; I exclude helper-kernel barrier routines because they are separate functions and not part of the target kernel body itself.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: From source and SASS, each team reads 16 input values (only `tx==0` lanes load `input[index_in]`) and 256 weights (`input_weights[index]`), both as 4-byte floats; the SASS shows corresponding `LDG.E` loads. The unique read footprint is therefore (16+256)*4 = 1088 bytes per team, and because teams touch disjoint regions totaling only about 4.46 MiB, well below the 40 MiB L2, this first streaming pass is effectively all compulsory DRAM reads: 1088*4096 = 4,456,448 bytes.

However the total unique write footprint is also only about 4.46 MiB, far below the 40 MiB L2 on A100, so these write-back cache lines need not be evicted during this first invocation; the defensible DRAM write estimate during the kernel is therefore 0 bytes.

prediction.gridSz_explanation: The kernel is the first `#pragma omp target teams` region at line 78 in bpnn_train_kernel. It is launched with `num_teams(num_blocks)` where `num_blocks = in / BLOCK_SIZE = 65536 / 16 = 4096`. The OpenMP runtime maps each team to one CUDA block, so gridSz.x = 4096. The SASS confirms S2R SR_CTAID.X is used as the team/block index.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The directive specifies `thread_limit(BLOCK_SIZE*BLOCK_SIZE) = thread_limit(256)`. The OpenMP runtime for clang on NVIDIA GPUs typically launches exactly the thread_limit number of threads per block. The SASS shows thread ID (SR_TID.X) being used with modulo 16 and divide by 16 to get tx and ty, consistent with 256 threads per block. However, the OpenMP runtime on clang/LLVM typically adds one extra warp for the "master" thread that handles team-level initialization, making the actual block size 256 + 32 = 288. The SASS code structure with the initial thread-0 check and the branching pattern at the beginning (checking R2 == 0 for initialization) and the later code path at .L_x_101 that sets up parallel execution with a wrapper function confirms this pattern. But looking more carefully at the SASS, the block size appears to be 256 based on the thread_limit directive - the runtime may or may not add extra threads. Given the SASS evidence showing R0 = 0x400 + 0x10 = 0x410 and various shared memory offset calculations, and the standard LLVM OpenMP runtime behavior, the block size is likely 256 (the thread_limit value).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
Looking at the SASS for the executed path, each of the 256 threads per block performs the following FP32 operations:

1. HFMA2 at 0x0090: This is executed only by thread 0 of each block for initialization - it's an FP16 instruction, not FP32.

2. FMUL at 0x0b40 (or 0x1e90 in the alternate path): weight_matrix[ty*WIDTH+tx] * input_node[ty] = 1 FMUL per thread. That's 256 threads × 4096 blocks = 1,048,576 FMULs.

3. The reduction loop iterates for i=1,2,4,8,16 (log2(16)=4 iterations, i=1,2,4,8,16 means 5 iterations but HEIGHT=16 so i goes 1,2,4,8,16). Looking at the SASS:
   - i=1 (power_two=1): FADD at 0x0d10 (R14+R14, which is effectively x+x). Every thread has ty%1==0, so all 256 threads execute. But wait - the SASS shows `FADD R18, R14, R14` which adds the value to itself. This corresponds to the first iteration where power_two=1, power_two/2=0, so weight_matrix[ty*WIDTH+tx] + weight_matrix[ty*WIDTH+tx]. All 256 threads execute this = 1 FADD each.
   - i=2 (power_two=2): Conditional on ty%2==0, which is checked via LOP3.LUT with mask 0x10 (bit 4 of R12, where R12 encodes ty). 128 threads execute FADD at 0x0f10.
   - i=4 (power_two=4): Conditional on ty%4==0, mask 0x30. 64 threads execute FADD at 0x10f0.
   - i=8 (power_two=8): Conditional on ty%8==0, mask 0x70. 32 threads execute FADD at 0x12d0.
   - i=16 (power_two=16): Conditional on ty%16==0, mask 0xf0. 16 threads execute FADD at 0x14b0.

Total FADDs per block in reduction: 256 + 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 = 496
Total FMULs per block: 256

Per block FP32 ops: 256 + 496 = 752
Total across 4096 blocks: 752 × 4096 = 3,080,192
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: No double-precision floating point operations are visible in the SASS for this kernel. All arithmetic is FP32 (FMUL, FADD). There are no DFMA, DMUL, DADD instructions.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The SASS shows one HFMA2 instruction at address 0x0090: `HFMA2.MMA R0, -RZ, RZ, 0, 5.9604644775390625e-08`. This is executed only by thread 0 of each block (guarded by P0 which checks R2 != 0, and the branch @P0 BRA skips past it for non-zero thread IDs). HFMA2 performs 2 packed FP16 FMA operations, each FMA = 2 FLOPs, so 4 FP16 FLOPs per HFMA2 instruction. With 4096 blocks, each having thread 0 execute this once: 4096 × 4 = 16,384 FP16 FLOPs.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation:
Each block reads from two global arrays:
1. input[] array: Each block reads 16 values (one per ty when tx==0) via LDG at 0x06e0. That's 16 × 4 = 64 bytes per block. But only threads with tx==0 (16 threads) load, and each loads one float. Across 4096 blocks: unique footprint = 65536 floats × 4 bytes = 262,144 bytes for input (indices 1 to 65536). However, each block reads a distinct set of 16 input values (HEIGHT*by+ty+1), so the total unique read footprint is 65536 × 4 = 262,144 bytes.

2. input_weights[] array: Each of 256 threads per block loads one float via LDG at 0x0920. That's 256 × 4 = 1024 bytes per block. Across 4096 blocks: 4096 × 256 × 4 = 4,194,304 bytes. The indices are distinct across blocks (different `by` values), so the unique footprint is 4,194,304 bytes.

Total unique read footprint: 262,144 + 4,194,304 = 4,456,448 bytes.

The L2 cache is 50 MB, which is much larger than this footprint. However, since this is the first kernel invocation, all data must be fetched from DRAM (cold cache). So DRAM bytes read ≈ 4,456,448 bytes. With cache line alignment (128-byte lines), there may be slight overhead, but the data is accessed fairly contiguously, so the estimate stays close to the unique footprint.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation:
Each block writes to two global arrays:
1. input_weights[] via STG at 0x1690/0x28b0: Each of 256 threads writes one float = 1024 bytes per block. Across 4096 blocks: 4,194,304 bytes.

2. partial_sum[] via STG at 0x1880/0x2a80: Only threads with tx==0 (16 threads per block) write, but looking more carefully, only threads where R13==0 (i.e., the lower 4 bits of the thread mapping are 0, meaning tx==0) write. That's 16 floats per block = 64 bytes. Across 4096 blocks: 262,144 bytes.

Total unique write footprint: 4,194,304 + 262,144 = 4,456,448 bytes.

The L2 cache is 50 MB, which is much larger than 4.5 MB. Since the L2 is a write-back cache, all writes will stay in L2 during this kernel invocation and won't be evicted to DRAM. Therefore DRAM bytes written ≈ 0.

1. Index computation: integer only, no FP.
2. `weight_matrix[ty*WIDTH+tx] = input_weights[index]` - load, no FP op.
3. `weight_matrix[ty*WIDTH+tx] = weight_matrix[ty*WIDTH+tx] * input_node[ty]` - 1 FP32 multiply per thread = 1,048,576 FP32 ops.
4. Reduction loop: `for (i=1; i<=HEIGHT; i*=2)` iterates with i=1,2,4,8,16, so 5 iterations. But only threads where `ty % power_two == 0` execute the addition. prediction.gridSz_explanation: The first invocation of the target OpenMP offload kernel is the first `#pragma omp target teams` region in `bpnn_train_kernel`. Host constant propagation from argv `65536` gives `in=65536`, `hid=16`, and `num_blocks=in/BLOCK_SIZE=65536/16=4096`; the directive explicitly requests `num_teams(num_blocks)`, so the first kernel launches 4096 teams in 1D.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The same first offload region uses `thread_limit(BLOCK_SIZE*BLOCK_SIZE)` with `BLOCK_SIZE=16`, so the requested team size is 256 threads. In this benchmark each thread maps to one `(ty,tx)` pair via `tx=tid%16`, `ty=tid/16`, so the effective block size is 256x1x1.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: In the first offload kernel, each of the 4096 teams has 256 threads. Every thread performs one FP32 multiply for `weight_matrix[...] * input_node[ty]`; then in the reduction loop `i=1,2,4,8,16`, the condition `ty % power_two == 0` is true for all threads at `i=1`, half the rows at `i=2`, one quarter at `i=4`, one eighth at `i=8`, and one sixteenth at `i=16`, yielding per-team adds of 256+128+64+32+16 = 496; total per-team FP32 ops = 256 muls + 496 adds = 752, and total kernel FP32 FLOPs = 4096*752 = 3,080,192. This source-level count ignores possible compiler-inserted helper instructions and counts only the taken arithmetic in the first kernel invocation.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: The first target kernel uses only `float` arrays and float arithmetic, with no `double` variables or double-precision math calls on the device path. Therefore no FP64 operations are attributable to the first invocation.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The kernel source contains no half-precision data types or explicit FP16 operations, and there is no evidence from source alone that the compiler would lower any executed arithmetic to packed FP16 instructions here. Thus the defensible estimate for FP16 FLOPs in the first invocation is zero.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Per team, the kernel reads 16 input values via the `tx==0` threads (16 floats = 64 B) and reads 256 `input_weights[index]` values (256 floats = 1024 B), for a unique read footprint of 1088 B per team. Across 4096 teams this is 4096*(64+1024)=4,456,448 B, and because each team touches disjoint portions of the large arrays with essentially no inter-team reuse while the overall footprint exceeds practical per-kernel reuse needs, DRAM read traffic is well approximated by this unique footprint.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The first kernel writes 256 updated `input_weights[index]` floats plus 16 `partial_sum[...]` floats per team, i.e. 272 floats = 1088 B per team. Across 4096 teams that is 4,456,448 B of unique write footprint; since this write set is only about 4.25 MiB, far smaller than the A100's 40 MiB L2, these dirty lines can remain resident in L2 during the kernel without eviction, so the estimated DRAM bytes written during this first invocation is effectively zero.
